why: A record written `as any` as the key of a Map<string, V> or the item of a Set<string> keeps its run-time value, an object, and a Map or Set compares objects by reference (SameValueZero): two records with equal fields are two keys. The type-assertion reading converted such a key by the record's value, ext_Any_as_string_Any(ext_Any_of_Rec_Rec(r)), so two records with equal fields gave one key, and lane A proved countByKey (size 2 in JavaScript) equal to a constant 1, setByKey (the Set mirror) likewise, and hasOther (has of an equal-fields record, false in JavaScript) equal to true: three false proofs (commit b8efb60f, the equal block, 3 FAILED). The reference-key and reference-equality guards read the asserted type, any, and saw no object; now a reference whose type an assertion erased is refused where it is compared by identity (common.mjs erasedReferenceSlot; the translator refuses reference-key and reference-equality, the lint reference-equality). The translator refuses the file, so lane A's result is read unit by unit through check.mjs: against candidate.ts lane B witnesses countByKey, setByKey, hasOther and countByNumber (n and String(n) are two keys); against refactor.ts (the same units, locals renamed, equal in JavaScript) lane B passes and lane A answers ASK naming reference-key (before the rule: PASS-proved). countByString keys by String(r), one string on both sides: lane A proves it (PASS-proved). Since lane w1b (design/w1b-opaque-statements.md) reference-key is graded: the refactor's units are read with an opaque step, which changes and compares a Map or Set after `new Map()` binds a reference, so the step is read in its unit's block (w1a's form); the renamed locals make the block's text another symbol, so lane A does not prove them (ASK:unproved), as before it refused them.
